term: Family Smoking Prevention and Tobacco Control Act of 2009
definition: The Family Smoking Prevention and Tobacco Control Act of 2009 implemented multiple wide-sweeping restrictions on the tobacco industry and gave the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) broad authority to regulate tobacco products. A few of the biggest restrictions include:  Requiring clearly displayed warnings on tobacco products of many health risks  Prevents the sale of tobacco products to children and marketing strategies that appeal to children like candy flavors  Prevents unsubstantiated claims of reduced risk to health on tobacco product containers
